title: Pre-cutover shadow parity report
description: data_collection/parity/{trading_day}.json (data-collector plan §6.2 step 4, alpha-engine-config-I10778). Written by `python -m shadow parity`, which diffs one standalone shadow run's output under staging/shadow/{trading_day}/ against the same trading day's v1 output, per key: row count, symbol set, schema, value tolerance. Read by nousergon-data/data_gate/evidence.py::read_parity as the `data.cutover_ready.parity` clause's evidence (alpha-engine-config-I10777). PRODUCER TEST: tests/test_shadow_parity.py. v2 (alpha-engine-config-I11351 / -I11352): adds the per-key `settling_bar` block, the report-level `prior_day_settled` block, `summary.settling_bar_keys`, a `dispatch` field on every `legs` entry, and turns `legs_known` from a bare boolean into one boolean PER DISPATCH GROUP. v1 documents stay valid and stay readable by the gate (evidence.PARITY_SCHEMA_VERSIONS). v3 (alpha-engine-config-I11203, Brian's ruling 2026-09-24): adds the `v1_cause` row verdict -- a difference PROVEN, by machine-checked evidence recorded inline on the row, to be caused on the v1 side -- with its `v1_cause` / `v1_cause_refused` blocks, `summary.v1_cause`, `prior_day_settled.v1_cause`, and `values.identity_breaches` on frame rows. Evidence kind `recompute_lineage` (a derived key proven through the inputs it was computed from, `lineage/D31/{trading_day}.json`) was added within v3: the kind enum widened, no field changed shape. v1 and v2 documents stay valid.

schema_version.description: v3 is what the producer writes today. v1 and v2 are retained because reports published before them carry those versions and the cutover gate still reads them; a bump that invalidated them would red the parity clause for a reason that is not a parity fact.

trading_day.description: The trading day BOTH sides were produced for. The whole point of the override is that this is the same day on both sides; the weaker fallback in plan §6.2 step 4 compares against the previous day.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp the comparison ran. The gate clause's as_of, and what makes a stale report visibly stale rather than silently reused.

shadow_prefix.description: The output root the shadow run was confined to. shadow/root.py::ShadowRoot.prefix is the single source of this string.

code_sha.description: The commit the comparison ran from, or the literal "unknown" when the checkout is not a git working tree.

met.description: TRUE only when every row's verdict is `match` or `v1_cause` (alpha-engine-config-I11203: proven v1-side, explained and counted apart). An unmeasurable, missing or in-region-only row is not parity evidence (plan §4.1 rule 2: UNMEASURABLE is never met), so it makes this false.

summary.description: Counts by verdict, plus `total` and `settling_bar_keys`. Every verdict in the row enum appears as a key. `settling_bar_keys` is NOT a verdict: it is how many of the `match` keys matched only because their trading-day cells were graded as a settling bar, and a reader rolling `summary` up into exception counts must skip it (data_gate.evidence.SUMMARY_NON_VERDICT_FIELDS, alpha-engine-config-I11351). `v1_cause` IS a verdict (v3): rows explained by proven v1-side evidence. A reader must count it apart from `match`, never inside it (data_gate.evidence.PARITY_PASSING_VERDICTS).

excluded_units.description: Units deliberately not compared, each with its reason. Present so the report's denominator is auditable: a unit missing from `keys` is either here or a finding.

class.description: hand_excluded: EXCLUDED_UNITS (a declared, reviewable exception). lifecycle: no live v1 producer for this unit's declared lifecycle. out_of_run_scope: the unit produced no run manifest under this shadow run — it was not part of the workload the run executed (alpha-engine-config-I10890).

legs.description: What the PRODUCER legs of this run did, as the dispatcher recorded them. EMPTY means the comparator was not told -- which is NOT a claim that every leg ran (see legs_known). alpha-engine-config-I11200. OPTIONAL in the schema, ALWAYS written by the producer: making it required would invalidate every report published before 2026-09-20, including the 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-18 reports the cutover gate currently reads. A report missing the field is pre-I11200, not a producer that declined to say. Both dispatches write the SAME report key: the second run rewrites the comparison and its own group's leg entries, and KEEPS the other group's (shadow.parity.merge_legs).

name.description: the dispatcher's leg name, e.g. post-market-data

dispatch.description: Which dispatch ran this leg: `sameday` is the 18:30 ET post-market run on day D, `morning` is the 07:45 ET D+1 run of v1's two morning legs for the previous session (alpha-engine-config-I11352). Absent on a pre-I11352 entry, which is attributed to `sameday` on the next merge because that is the only dispatch that existed when it was written.

oneOf.description: v1 form: one bare boolean for the whole report.
v2 form: one boolean PER DISPATCH GROUP.

legs_known.description: Whether this report was told what the producer legs did. v2 reports it per dispatch group, because the same-day and morning dispatches write the same report and one bare boolean could not say the morning legs had not run yet without also erasing the same-day ones. A reader must NOT treat false as 'every leg succeeded' -- distinguishing those is why the field exists.

prior_day_settled.description: Deliverable 2 of alpha-engine-config-I11351: whether the bars the PREVIOUS trading day's report could only record as settling are, by now, settled on both sides. Built by reading parity/{previous trading day}.json and re-reading this report's own strict grading of that day's row. `available: false` names why the previous report was not read -- an absent block would be indistinguishable from 'nothing was unsettled'. OPTIONAL in the schema for the same reason `legs` is: v1 reports predate it.

settled.description: Keys whose previous-day row is now inside the strict band.

unsettled.description: Keys still breaching on that row -- a REAL producer difference the settling-bar grading deferred rather than forgave.

unmeasurable_reasons.description: Per reason: count, why, and up to ten example keys. A `same_day_snapshot` artifact is overwritten in place and can never be re-graded this way without a versioned read (`overwritten_in_place`, alpha-engine-config-I11360 deliverable 2) -- a property of the artifact, published rather than hidden by a shrinking denominator. A `key_date` artifact IS re-graded, via each key's own `prior_day_settled` field (alpha-engine-config-I11360); `prior_pair_unreadable` names the rare case where that re-grade itself came back neither match nor mismatch.

v1_cause.description: Re-graded D-1 pairs whose every breach is PROVEN to be v1's frozen, provisional D-1 file (v1's manifest stamps it bar_settlement: provisional, the shadow's settled). Neither settled nor unsettled: explained, and never counted in `unsettled` (alpha-engine-config-I11203).

gate_dispatch.description: alpha-engine-config-I11361: whether publishing this report dispatched the data-gate.yml read (trigger `parity-published`) for its trading day. Written only by `shadow parity --dispatch-gate`, i.e. the scheduled same-day and morning dispatches; absent on a manual or replay run, which never asked for a dispatch. `ok: false` carries the reason and is never fatal: the two post-publish crons read the same report as the backstop.

dispatched_at.description: UTC ISO time the dispatch was accepted (HTTP 204); null when `ok` is false.

key.description: The LIVE key (or, for an unaddressable declaration, the descriptor's own text). The shadow side is this key under `shadow_prefix`, carried in `shadow_key`.

shadow_library.description: For an ArcticDB row: the shadow library the run wrote, which an in-region comparator diffs against the live library named in `key`.

unit_ids.description: Every unit declaring this write. Two units on one key (D17/D19 on staging/daily_closes) is one comparison attributed to both.

verdict.description: `in_region_only` is its own verdict rather than a flavour of `unmeasurable` because it names a DIFFERENT next action: run the comparator in-region, not fix a read. `live_superseded` (alpha-engine-config-I10892): v1's run manifest for this trading day records an ETag the live key no longer carries, and no retained VersionId to fetch the recorded object by — the live object belongs to a later run, so it is not evidence either way. Never met. `not_applicable` (alpha-engine-config-I11231): the owning unit's OWN shadow run manifest for the trading day records `status: not_applicable` with a declared reason (e.g. `no_new_data_declared` on an immutable-date artifact) — v1 wrote the key and the shadow correctly did not, so there is nothing to diff. Its next action is 'read the declaration', not 'fix the producer', which is why it is not a flavour of `shadow_missing`. Never met: a declared no-op is not parity evidence either. `v1_cause` (alpha-engine-config-I11203, Brian's ruling 2026-09-24): every breach on the key is explained by machine-checked evidence, recorded in the row's `v1_cause.evidence`, that its cause is on the v1 side -- v1's own manifest stamps the bar `bar_settlement: provisional` while the shadow's stamps it `settled` (numeric breaches of a key_date key only), or the vendor published the shadow's extra trailing observations after v1's recorded fetch start. Schema, membership, coverage, row count and identity-field differences are never explained. Met, but counted apart from `match`.

live_version.description: Which live object was graded, against v1's run manifest for the trading day (alpha-engine-config-I10892). `basis`: `current_matches_manifest` (the current object IS the recorded one), `manifest_version_id` (the recorded VersionId was fetched), `superseded_no_version_id`, `recorded_version_not_retained`, or `unrecorded` (no manifest record carrying an etag — graded against the current object, as before).

identity_breaches.description: Frame rows only: how many of `breaches` are NOT a numeric move (a date, a label, a duplicate row key). Never explainable as v1_cause (alpha-engine-config-I11203).

provenance_diffs.description: Differences confined to fields the resolved contract marks `x-provenance` (alpha-engine-config-I10894) — e.g. `revision`, `fetched_at`. Reported as information; NEVER counted in `values.breaches` and never met-breaking.

settling_bar.description: The cells of this key that fall on the report's OWN trading day, whose bar the vendor was still settling when the two sides fetched it (alpha-engine-config-I11351). Recorded here and NEVER counted in `values.breaches`, so a key breaching only on that bar grades `match`. This is not a wider tolerance: `x-vendor-live.band` is untouched, and membership, schema, row count and coverage stay strict for every row including the trading day -- a missing or extra trading-day row is still a mismatch. A key with a settling_bar block AND a strict breach on an earlier row is still `mismatch`. Present only when the key's own contract declares an `x-settling-bar` basis AND that basis applies to this report. Under `row_date` and `key_date` only a NUMERIC move settles (a price, a volume, a derived indicator); an identity field that differs (`bar_date`, a currency, a label) is a strict breach on the trading day too (alpha-engine-config-I11551).

basis.description: row_date: the artifact is indexed by bar date and only the row equal to trading_day is settling (reference/price_cache/*.parquet); a JSON series document declares where each row's date is in its contract's `x-settling-bar.row_dates` and a row settles only when both sides date it trading_day (market_data/close_history/consolidated.json, `$.series.*[*][0]`, alpha-engine-config-I11551). key_date: the artifact is indexed by ticker and its KEY names one trading day, so the whole file is that day's bar (staging/daily_closes/{date}.parquet, features/{date}/*.parquet, market_data/eod_closes/{date}.json). same_day_snapshot: an undated, overwritten-in-place artifact whose whole content is a same-day derivation of the session's bar (market_data/technicals/latest.json).

examples.description: Up to ten, each carrying both sides (frames) or the rendered diff and its JSON path (documents).

max_rel.description: Largest relative move over the settling cells, or null when none was computable -- never 0.0, which would read as 'measured, and it did not move'.

settling_bar_declaration_problem.description: A contract declared `x-settling-bar.basis: row_date` on a JSON key without an `x-settling-bar.row_dates` entry naming where that key's row dates are. Recorded rather than silently applied or silently dropped: it means the contract and the artifact disagree. The contract loader never produces this state (a JSON template a row_date contract does not name carries no settling bar at all), so its appearance means a hand-built contract.

prior_day.description: This report's STRICT grading of the previous trading day's row -- the bar the previous report could only record as settling. Present only on a `row_date` key, the only shape carrying that history -- a parquet frame's dated index, or a JSON series document's declared `row_dates` (alpha-engine-config-I11551). `prior_day_settled` rolls these up.

prior_day_settled.description: This report's STRICT re-grade of the D-1-dated key pair for a `key_date` key -- the whole artifact yesterday's report could only record as settling (alpha-engine-config-I11360). Present only on the CURRENT (D-dated) row for a key whose settling_bar.basis is `key_date`; the D-1 pair itself is read from the live D-1 key and the D-1 SHADOW RUN's own output, never today's shadow root. `data_gate.evidence.SUMMARY_NON_VERDICT_FIELDS` and `ParityReport.summary`/`met` are unaffected by this field -- it never becomes a second row or a second verdict for the D key.

available.description: True only when the D-1 pair produced an ordinary strict match/mismatch outcome.

verdict.description: The underlying KeyResult verdict the D-1 pair graded as (match, mismatch, live_missing, shadow_missing, both_missing, unmeasurable, live_superseded, not_applicable).

settled.description: true when the D-1 pair matched under the contract's own band, false when it mismatched, null when `available` is false -- never a substituted false for an unmeasured pair.

shadow_run_status.description: For a key with no shadow object: what each owning unit's shadow run manifest for the trading day recorded. Present so a reader can tell a declared no-op from a failed leg from an unexplained gap without going to find the manifest (alpha-engine-config-I11231).

v1_cause.description: Present only on a `v1_cause` row: the evidence, one entry per explained breach group, each naming its kind and the manifest facts it was checked against.

kind.description: `recompute_lineage` (alpha-engine-config-I11203): a DERIVED key (D31's `features/{D}/*.parquet`), which stamps no settlement of its own. `shadow recompute-lineage` re-ran one feature code over the inputs v1's and the shadow's D31 each RECORDED and got each side's published bytes back exactly (sha256 on both sides, bound to the objects this report graded); every recorded input whose content differs between the runs (`differing_inputs`) was itself graded `v1_cause` under its own key's comparison at report time. The evidence chains; it is never assumed.

scope.description: `v1_bar_provisional` only. Absent: the whole key is stamped provisional on v1's side and settled on the shadow's. `rows` (alpha-engine-config-I11563): the whole-key stamp is ambiguous because a run carried some rows from an earlier write, and EVERY row holding a numeric breach was proven provisional on v1's side and settled on the shadow's, row by row. `rows` lists up to 25 of them with the manifests each reading was followed through; `rows_explained` counts all.

v1_cause_refused.description: On every `mismatch` row graded for v1_cause: why it is not `v1_cause` (up to ten), whether or not any v1-side evidence was found (alpha-engine-config-I11563; before it, a row with no evidence at all carried no reason). An almost-proof is published, never silently discarded.

failure_attribution.description: For a key with no shadow object whose owning unit's shadow run FAILED: whether that failure is this key's cause, read from the manifest's per-key `write_refused` record. `refused_this_key`: the run named this key. `not_this_key`: the run's COMPLETE refusal list does not name it, so the failure does not explain the absence. `truncated` / `unrecorded`: the run's list cannot rule the key in or out (alpha-engine-config-I11547).
